grade.first_issue: The first incorrect assertion is that forcing both children to contain an angle in S yields victory “in one move.” An angle kθ with k>1 is not terminal; it only gives a position from which the earlier induction guarantees a later win. This is non-load-bearing, so Rule C does not impose a cap.
grade.summary: The classification θ=180°/n for integers n≥2 is correctly proved. The interval construction makes both children contain positive integral multiples of θ, and the initial induction then gives finite winning strategies. The converse correctly establishes the safe-triangle invariant through all four cases and supplies a safe equilateral starting triangle. The only flaw is the false one-move bound; replacing it by “after one move both possible children are winning positions” completes the proof.
strengths: Valid induction showing that a triangle containing kθ is a winning position.
The interval argument correctly handles positivity, integrality, and the exceptional acute n=2 case.
The four-case invariant argument in the converse is complete.
The equilateral triangle is correctly shown to be safe whenever θ is not 180°/n.

errors.description: The claim that Mulan always wins in at most one move is false because S contains nonterminal multiples kθ. For example, with θ=60° and triangle (70°,55°,55°), the construction can leave Shan-Yu a child containing 120° but no 60°. The earlier induction nevertheless guarantees a finite subsequent win, so the requested result remains established.
